verdictStatement: All three findings v4 set out to repair are genuinely repaired, and the S-1 repair is better than what I asked for: rather than repointing the schema citation to a newer head, v4 removes the currency claim altogether and says so out loud ('This is not a live-head or in-review claim; a later successor may exist'), which immunises the entry against the head moving again — and the head HAS moved again, to v9. What withholds acceptance is that the v4 delta's own closure discipline does not hold on its own bytes. basedOn.method asserts 'Every path neither the substantive roster nor succession metadata names is unchanged from v3'; /reviewGuidance is named by neither list and is not unchanged from v3 — three items were appended, one of which is literally the instruction to attack silent v3-to-v4 paths. And the retained v2 repair roster still reads 'governingSources now digest … and current schemas.v7', which is both the time-indexed predicate class this delta exists to remove and a false statement about v4's own governing sources, since v4 removed schemas.v7 and cites v9 instead. Both are one-line fixes. Neither touches a rule, a window, an authority, or an attribution.

shouldFix.title: /reviewGuidance changed and is named by neither roster, falsifying basedOn.method's explicit closure sentence

measurement.theClosureClaim: basedOn.method ends: 'Every path neither the substantive roster nor succession metadata names is unchanged from v3.' The substantive roster names /recordedInputs/governingSources, /lockJoin and /honestyRepairsFromV3. The succession-metadata list names /artifact, /version, /basedOn and /honestyRepairsFromV3. /reviewGuidance appears in neither — I checked by string search across both rosters, not by eye.
measurement.theActualChange: reviewGuidance.forTheIndependentReviewer grew from 11 items to 14. The three appended items are: 'Attack time-indexed current/under review claims about a schema successor.', 'Attack treating delivery.v4's own NOT APPLIED field as the application warrant.', and 'Attack any silent v3-to-v4 path outside honestyRepairsFromV3 / basedOn.method.'
measurement.soTheClaimIsFalse: A path neither list names is NOT unchanged from v3. The universal quantifier is refuted by a single measured counterexample.

shouldFix.aSecondDefectInTheSameField: While three items were appended, the stale item at index 5 was left as-is: 'Attack treating schemas.v7 (or v6) as accepted; citing them does not accept DR-103.' Neither v6 nor v7 is cited anywhere in v4 — the S-1 repair removed the v7 entry from governingSources and replaced the v6/v7 parenthetical in lockJoin. So the field was edited in the same pass that orphaned its own reference, and neither the edit nor the orphan is disclosed.
shouldFix.whyShouldFixAndNotBlocker: I record plainly that the added content is non-authority-bearing and points the wrong way for a smuggler: it instructs reviewers to attack MORE, including to attack exactly this class of omission. Nothing about the contract's meaning, attribution, windows or authority moves. That is why this is not a blocker. But it is not advisory either: the closed-roster property is the specific thing v3 and v4 were built to establish, the dispatch names this attack explicitly, and a coordinator who bounds their re-read by the roster would not re-read reviewGuidance. A closure sentence that is false on the artifact's own bytes cannot be relied on at all, regardless of how benign the omitted change happens to be.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Add /reviewGuidance to the substantive roster in basedOn.method and name it in honestyRepairsFromV3 (three attack lines appended for S-1, S-2 and the v3→v4 silent-path check). While there, refresh the orphaned item 5 to name the successor v4 actually cites, or restate it without a version number.

advisories.detail: The substantive roster reads '/recordedInputs/governingSources (…), /lockJoin (…), /honestyRepairsFromV3.' The next sentence reads 'Succession metadata (not substantive): /artifact, /version, /basedOn, /honestyRepairsFromV3.' The same path is on both lists, and the second is expressly labelled 'not substantive'. The artifact therefore classifies one path two contradictory ways in the field my v3 ADV-1 asked to be made precise.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The path is disclosed either way, so the closed-roster property is not damaged by this particular defect and I reproduced the roster without ambiguity. Recorded so it can be closed cheaply alongside S-1, since both are edits to the same field.
advisories.suggestedFix: Drop /honestyRepairsFromV3 from one of the two lists. Succession metadata is the more natural home, on the same footing as /basedOn.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed: That the S-1 repair merely repointed the citation and would go stale again. It did not — v4 removes the currency predicate rather than refreshing it, and explicitly says a later successor may exist. The lineage did move again (v9 is on disk, v8 already superseded) and the entry survived that move intact.
That the freeze citation was approximate. It is not: section 3's heading is at line 285 and the DELIVERY row at line 385 falls inside it, reading 'Applied 2026-08-05'.

That removing schemas.v7 from governingSources orphaned a load-bearing claim. lockJoin was updated in the same pass and is consistent. The only orphan is an attack instruction in reviewGuidance, folded into S-1.

That the delivery role now overstates by calling delivery.v4 'the DELIVERY bytes applied 2026-08-05'. It does not overstate: it names the freeze as the recorder in the same sentence and discloses the artifact's own contrary field.

That some standing property silently regressed while attention was on the two repairs. Whole-key diff plus element-by-element surface comparison: twenty keys including all eight surfaces are byte-identical to v3.
That a v3 finding from either reviewer survives unrepaired. None does — see M-13.
coordinatorNote: v4 is close, and the way it closed S-1 is the part worth keeping: it removed the time-indexed claim rather than refreshing it, which is the only repair of that shape that survives a lineage that keeps moving — and it did move again during this review. Both remaining SHOULD-FIX items are self-description defects in the change-disclosure machinery, not defects in the contract: one path changed outside a roster that claims to be closed, and one superseded roster retained without the 'Historical' label the artifact already uses elsewhere. Neither alters a surface, a window, an attribution, or an authority, and both are single-line edits confined to /basedOn/method, /honestyRepairsFromV3, /reviewGuidance and the name of /honestyRepairsFromV2. I note for the record that Codex accepted v3 where I did not; on v4 the two findings below are objective measurements rather than severity judgements — the closure sentence is refuted by a counterexample, and the retained roster is false about the artifact's own governing sources. DR-111 remains OPEN. Nothing here marks it SATISFIED and no implementation is authorized.
